2.3.7 Assessment Strategies 
Assessments allow students to understand what they do and do not know; the 
primary goals of an assessment should be to provide feedback and gauge the 
students current level of understanding for a certain topic. 
 (Barana, et al., 2019) highlights two key factors when implementing digital 
assessments. First, assessments should go beyond just grading; and should 
additionally aid students to learn from their mistakes by offering hints and or 
explanations. Secondly, they recommend using assessments to analyse the 
learning material, the data will aid the teacher or content creator in making the 
course more effective and engaging. 
By meta-analysis by (Panadero, et al., 2017), largely agrees with (Barana, et 
al., 2019), and goes into further details on assessment implementation. 
(Panadero, et al., 2017) recommends the following in the context of an 
eLearning platform to improve learning and student motivation: 
1. Self-Assessment and feedback mechanisms: Should allow students 
to assess their understanding and performance; which could be 
implemented with prompts to aid students in areas for improvement, or 
with reflective questions. 
2.  Self-Regulated learning support: Students should be able to set their 
own goals and monitor their progress. 
3. Goal setting: Students should have simple and clear criteria for success. 
4. Personalisation: An assessments level of difficulty should be based on 
the student’s current level of education, or based on their personal goals.
